claims.explanation: Zardaverine is a dual PDE3/PDE4 inhibitor that raises cAMP, and its selectivity likely reflects dependence on cAMP signaling for survival. Lines with BRAF mutations, especially melanoma, are sensitized, possibly because BRAF-mutant cells have elevated MAPK-driven PDE4 expression and rely on cAMP for feedback. Conversely, PTEN loss and high PI3K/AKT signaling protect cells by promoting survival independent of cAMP.

features.basis: Enriched in selectively killed melanoma lines; BRAF-mutant cells may depend on PDE4-mediated cAMP regulation.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling, reducing dependence on cAMP-regulated pathways.
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines (lung, pancreas, soft tissue), possibly linking oncogenic RAS to PDE4 dependence.
Zardaverine targets PDE4D; high expression may increase drug sensitivity by elevating cAMP upon inhibition.
Zardaverine also inhibits PDE3; high PDE3A expression could contribute to cAMP elevation and sensitivity.
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines, but also in resistant lines, so this is weak evidence.
STK11 mutations appear in some sensitive lines (lung, melanoma, glioma), possibly altering AMPK/cAMP crosstalk.
ATM mutations are present in several sensitive lines, but the mechanism is unclear.
CTNNB1 mutations appear in some sensitive lines, but also in resistant lines, so this is weak evidence.
PIK3CA mutations are more frequent in resistant lines, suggesting PI3K activation may protect against cAMP-mediated death.
CDKN2A mutations are common in resistant lines, but the mechanism is unclear.
SMAD4 mutations appear in several resistant lines, but the mechanism is unclear.
